metadata.description: Where the AegisShield code does something that lines up with a NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control. Written by the project's maintainers from the code. It is not an assessment, has not been reviewed by a third party, and is not a statement of compliance with SP 800-53 or with any program built on it.

scope_values.application: A safeguard in the application itself.
scope_values.capability: A feature that can help a user's organization with its own work on the control. The application does not meet the control for that organization.

metadata.evidence_rule: Each location names a file in this repository and the functions, classes, or methods in it (Class.method) that carry the behavior. A test in tests/aegisshield/services/test_nist_800_53_service.py fails when a file or name no longer exists.

controls.description: Protects the content of the API keys the app holds for outside services (OpenAI, NVD, AlienVault OTX). It does not authenticate the app's own users; the app has none.
evidence: A visitor's keys are entered in masked inputs and kept only in that visitor's Streamlit session state; the input is emptied once a key is stored.
Operator keys for NVD and OTX are read from Streamlit secrets; there is no operator fallback for the OpenAI key.
Keys are passed by value into the job that needs them; the job runner drops the job function, and with it the key, as soon as the job ends.
Log lines for failed jobs pass through redact_keys; OpenAI SDK errors are re-raised without their message, and the client's repr shows no key.

controls.description: One Streamlit process serves every visitor. The job runner and the default workspace store keep one visitor's work out of reach of another visitor in that process.
evidence: Job ids come from secrets.token_urlsafe(32) and the runner has no way to list jobs; a session sees only the jobs whose ids it holds.

While a job runs, its id is also in the page URL (?run=) so a reload can find it; anyone with that URL can open the job while it runs and for 30 seconds after it ends, and each page removes the id from the URL when the job finishes, fails, is cancelled, or is no longer held.
Finished jobs are dropped after a time to live (15 minutes by default), and a job still running at the job timeout is marked failed and told to stop.

At most AEGIS_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS jobs (4 by default) run at once in the process, and at most 1 packet capture analysis, 2 vulnerability lookups, 2 policies, and 3 threat models at once across all visitors; a refused job gets a fixed sentence.

By default the workspace is a MappingStore over the visitor's own session state; the on-disk FileStore, one file shared by everyone, is used only when the operator sets AEGIS_DATA_DIR, and the app logs a warning when it is.

controls.description: Checks uploads, imported files, and visitor text on the server before they are used, whatever the browser sent.
evidence: The Streamlit server accepts at most 25 MB per upload (maxUploadSize in .streamlit/config.toml).
A packet capture is checked for size (25 MB), extension (.pcap or .pcapng), and pcap or pcapng magic bytes before it is written to disk.
An architecture image (10 MB) and a workspace import (10 MB) are refused by their reported size before they are read; an image must be a PNG or JPEG by its own first bytes.
A workspace import is refused when its schema version, keys, types, or record ids are wrong.

Text limits are enforced on the server: description 20,000 characters, diagram description 10,000, profile values 200 characters and lists 500 items (the threat-model request refuses anything longer), version strings 32 characters, and edited policy text 200,000 characters.
Visitor text has control and invisible characters (including bidirectional controls) removed; model names from the environment must be in AVAILABLE_MODELS.

controls.description: Error messages shown to a visitor are fixed sentences from the app's own code that never carry provider text, a library's exception text, or keys. Detail goes to the server log only.
evidence: A failed job's error is a fixed sentence chosen by exception class, or one of its service's own fixed sentences (the PCAP service's, the safeguards', the scan service's); the exception's class and message are logged with key-shaped text redacted.
OpenAI SDK errors are logged by class and HTTP status and re-raised as a fixed LLMError without the original message.
tshark failures are logged on the server and shown as fixed sentences.
The Streamlit configuration sets showErrorDetails to none, so an unexpected exception is not shown in the page.

controls.description: Treats model output and visitor text as untrusted when it is placed into exports, so it cannot add markup, scripts, or outside resources of its own.
evidence: Every string placed into the HTML export is escaped; markdown is rendered with raw HTML escaped and images reduced to their alt text.

In the HTML export and the PDFs, links in model and visitor text stay links only for http, https, mailto, and in-page fragments; any other link becomes plain text. In the page, model text that names a javascript:, vbscript:, data:, or file: scheme anywhere has every link shown as plain text (kit.model_markdown).
The HTML export carries a Content-Security-Policy that allows no scripts and no outside resources.

Every PDF the app makes (threat-model report and policy) goes through one renderer whose resource policy refuses every network fetch and every local file read; only images embedded in the document load.
Packet-derived text is escaped in the PCAP markdown report.

controls.description: The threat-model wizard drafts a STRIDE threat model, an attack tree, a DREAD assessment, mitigations, and test cases for a system the user describes. The output is model-generated and is a draft for a person to review; it is input to a risk assessment, not one.
evidence: run_threat_model is the one entry point the wizard submits to the job runner; it runs the linear or the agentic path.
The DREAD assessment scores each threat on the five DREAD factors.

controls.description: Brings public threat information into the user's view: AlienVault OTX reports, and the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog in the vulnerability lookup. These are read-only lookups of public sources; the app shares nothing back.
evidence: With an OTX key, a threat-model run fetches recent OTX reports for the selected industry sector, and a vulnerability lookup fetches OTX reports for each technology.
The vulnerability lookup marks CVEs that are in the CISA KEV catalog.
